scenes.narration: AI doesn't think. It does math. Billions of times.
Welcome to FredsDesk, lesson three. In one minute, you'll see how a neural network makes a decision.
A neural network is layers of simple units, called neurons, that pass numbers to each other, and learn from examples.
scenes.definition: Layers of simple units that pass numbers to each other, and learn from examples.

scenes.narration: Here, a photo goes in on the left. Each neuron multiplies its inputs by weights, adds them up, and passes the result forward. Layer by layer, the signal builds, until the last layer makes a guess: cat, ninety-two percent.
scenes.note: Illustrative · real networks have millions to billions of neurons

scenes.narration: GPT-3, released in twenty twenty, has a hundred and seventy-five billion of these weights. Training nudges every one of them until the guesses get good.
scenes.label: weights in GPT-3
scenes.sub: Training adjusts every one until predictions improve.

scenes.narration: Quick recap. One: a neural network is layers of simple units. Two: it multiplies, adds, and passes signals forward. Three: training tunes the weights until answers improve.
Quiz time! What are weights: A, adjustable numbers, or B, stored photos? Answer in the comments. Tomorrow: what is a token? Follow FredsDesk, and see you at the desk.
scenes.question: What are weights?
